Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 43

“Full of desires, intent on heaven, they urge many specific rites for the sake of pleasure and power, yielding rebirth as the fruit of action.”

The critique sharpens: this is religion pursued as a transaction for better enjoyments. Krishna's objection is that it works — it delivers exactly the recurring births its practitioners bargained for.
